name: Shillong
description: Capital city and headquarters of East Khasi Hills district, known as the Scotland of the East. Hill station with colonial architecture, lakes, markets, and panoramic views.
facts: Named after the deity U-Lei Shillong
Educational hub with IIM Shillong and other institutions
Nearest major airport and rail in Guwahati

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Sub-divisional town in East Khasi Hills, historically one of the wettest places on Earth. Famous for waterfalls, living root bridges, caves, and dramatic plateau views over Bangladesh plains.
facts: Local name Sohra, traditional capital of Hima Sohra
Holds records for highest rainfall in a month and year
Gateway to Nohkalikai Falls and Nongriat bridges

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India, dropping about 340 m from the Cherrapunji plateau into a turquoise pool. Located near Sohra in East Khasi Hills with cultural legend of Ka Likai.
facts: Named after legend of woman Ka Likai

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong in East Khasi Hills. Locally known as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew, surrounded by lush greenery and ferns.
facts: About 12 km from Shillong city center

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at about 1,965 m, 10 km south of Shillong. Offers panoramic views of the city, hills, and Bangladesh plains on clear days. Sacred to Khasi people.
facts: Sacred site for U Lei Shillong
Requires ID for entry near radar station

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Known as Asia's cleanest village in East Khasi Hills near the Bangladesh border. Features living root bridges, sky viewpoint, balancing rock, and community-led eco-tourism.
facts: Declared cleanest village in Asia by Discover India in 2003

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tier living root bridge woven from Ficus elastica roots in Nongriat village, East Khasi Hills. Requires trek of about 3,500 steps from Tyrna near Sohra.
facts: Part of living root bridges cultural landscape

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove preserved by Khasi traditions near Mawphlang village in East Khasi Hills. Biodiversity hotspot with centuries-old trees, monoliths, and spiritual significance.
facts: No removal of anything from the forest
Home to rare plants and orchids

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon viewpoint in East Khasi Hills near Smit, offering sweeping views of deep valleys and hills. Known as the end of the hills in Khasi.
facts: Steep descent possible to valley villages

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone cave near Sohra in East Khasi Hills with stalactites, stalagmites, and fossils. Short route suitable for most visitors.
facts: Named from Khasi for oath stone
Often paired with Seven Sisters Falls

name: Jowai
description: Headquarters of West Jaintia Hills district and cultural hub of the Pnar (Jaintia) people. Situated on a plateau at about 1,380 m, encircled by the Myntdu River, with markets, Presbyterian Church, and access to nearby attractions.
facts: Surrounded on three sides by Myntdu River

name: Krang Suri Falls
description: Iconic waterfall in Amlarem subdivision with vivid turquoise-blue pool, limestone cliffs, and dense forest. Multi-tiered cascade ideal for swimming (with life jackets), photography, and short trek.

name: Nartiang Monoliths
description: Largest collection of megalithic monoliths (menhirs and dolmens) in Meghalaya, erected 1500–1835 by Jaintia kings and clans in Nartiang, former summer capital. Tallest menhir ~8 m, often called Stonehenge of the Northeast.
facts: Includes menhirs dedicated to male ancestors and dolmens to females

name: Nartiang Durga Temple
description: Ancient ~600-year-old temple in Nartiang, one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, where the left thigh of Goddess Sati is believed to have fallen. Adjacent to summer palace ruins of Jaintia kings.
facts: Near monoliths and summer palace ruins

name: Thadlaskein Lake
description: Man-made historical lake near Mukhla on NH-6, legendarily dug overnight by followers of rebel general Sajar Nangli using bow tips. Popular picnic and boating spot surrounded by meadows.
facts: Also known as Pung Sajar Nangli

name: Tyrshi Falls
description: Cascading waterfall near Jowai on the Shillong-Jowai road, often compared to Elephant Falls. Features an arched bridge viewpoint over paddy fields, with multi-tiered flow.
facts: Local name linked to warrior Tyrshi

name: Dawki and Umngot River
description: Border town on Indo-Bangladesh frontier famous for the crystal-clear Umngot (Dawki) River where boats appear to float on air. Suspension bridge, boating, and views into Bangladesh plains.
facts: Umngot often called India's cleanest river

name: Shnongpdeng
description: Riverside village near Dawki on the Umngot River, quieter alternative for camping, kayaking, cliff jumping, zip-lining, and swimming in clear waters with fewer crowds.

name: Syntu Ksiar
description: Riverside meadow and pool on the Myntdu River near Jowai, meaning 'golden flower'. Historical site of freedom struggle with Kiang Nangbah memorial; popular for picnics and walks.
facts: Monument to freedom fighter U Kiang Nangbah

name: Ialong Park
description: Eco-park and sacred grove about 8 km from Jowai, overlooking Pynthorwah Valley and Myntdu River. Features walking trails, viewpoints, and community tourism facilities.

name: Phe Phe Falls
description: Two-tiered hidden waterfall near Shkentalang/Jarain village, known as Paradise Falls, with turquoise plunge pool. Requires moderate trek through forest and bamboo; less crowded offbeat gem.

name: Thlu Muwi (Megalithic Bridge)
description: Historical megalithic stone bridge over Muwi stream near Jowai-Dawki road, built by Jaintia warriors for kings traveling to Nartiang summer capital. Adjacent Muwi waterfalls add scenic value.
facts: About 16 km from Jowai on Dawki road
